Table 17 contains every one of the 43 budget rows from 20 complete main trainings and 29 task/color strata. The missing drawer PPO only controls and missing 456-only controls in the repeated LIV cube trainings remain missing. For R164/R166/R167/R165/R184, supplemental R168/R170/R171/R172/R189 supply identical-456-head only policies with matched feedback budgets. K.5 Initial-policy Semantic Misranking

Using only initial-policy trajectories, we computed the success–all-failure area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC; S1), the success–wrong-object AUROC (S2), a standardized wrong-minus-success score margin (S3) and top-quartile wrong-object enrichment (S4). We compared them with the subsequent Δ​W\Delta W across the 29 distinct induction strata from 20 training histories; every metric is defined in every stratum. The analysis is retrospective: “initial-policy” identifies the policy distribution, not the collection date. Semantic misranking tracks amplification. The Spearman correlation of S2 with Δ​W\Delta W is −.82​[−.91,−.68]-.82\,[-.91,-.68] (training-history bootstrap), against −.34​[−.63,+.05]-.34\,[-.63,+.05] for the generic S1; S3 and S4 agree (Table 18). Computing each metric and Δ​W\Delta W on disjoint halves of the initial-policy panel gives −.74​[−.82,−.61]-.74\,[-.82,-.61] for S2 and −.31​[−.58,+.08]-.31\,[-.58,+.08] for S1: the association persists without direct reuse of baseline observations, although this does not remove family/color confounding. The association is carried by differences between task/critic families and between colors: it is absent within both drawer families, and four near-color LIV strata have S2 below .5 without amplification (Section K.5). We read it as a retrospective description of these settings, not a validated predictor.

Metric definitions and analysis.

Each of the 29 strata contributes its initial-policy (UU) endpoint executions, scored by its original critic in native units; post-optimization trajectories never enter a static metric. With SS, WW and FF the successes, wrong-object failures and all failures of a stratum, the metrics are: (S1) AUROC of SS versus FF; (S2) AUROC of SS versus WW; (S3) (r¯W−r¯S)/sr(\bar{r}_{W}-\bar{r}_{S})/s_{r}, with srs_{r} the population standard deviation of all UU scores; and (S4) the wrong-object fraction among episodes at or above the 75th score percentile minus its overall fraction. AUROCs count ties as one half. An AUROC or margin is unavailable when a required class has fewer than three episodes, and S3 is unavailable when the scores have no variance. The response is Δ​W\Delta W, the critic-minus-uniform change in wrong-object rate. Intervals resample the 20 training histories with all of their strata (20,000 draws). These definitions and the bootstrap were committed before any stratum metric was computed. The disjoint-halves analysis and the difference row of Table 18 were added afterwards, each declared before its own computation.

Shared baseline.

Both a static metric and Δ​W\Delta W depend on the same UU episodes. Each panel was therefore split into halves by identifiers alone: whole evaluation banks alternate for the drawer strata, and seeds alternate within each design cell for stacking. Metrics come from one half’s UU episodes and Δ​W\Delta W from the other half’s paired executions, in both directions, averaged. Halving leaves S2 unavailable in 4 and 2 strata. The negative association persists when the static metric and the amplification estimate use disjoint baseline halves. This reduces direct reuse of baseline observations but does not eliminate family/color confounding, establish prospective prediction, or quantify all sources of dependence.

Dependence and scope.

No evaluation seed set is shared across training histories. The strata of one history share its initial policy, seeds and first feedback and are resampled together. After removing the four task/critic family means, the correlations are −.77-.77 for S2 and −.47-.47 for S1. Within families the association appears only in the two stacking families, where it largely reflects the near/distinct contrast. The two drawer families show none: their S2 values span narrow ranges. A bootstrap over the four families cannot support an interval. Exceptions:

  • •

    The generic AUROC also flags the distinct-color LIV strata (0.15–0.36).

  • •

    Four near-color LIV strata have S2 of 0.40–0.48 without amplification.

  • •

    Two Robometer stacking strata show wrong-object amplification together with a success gain.

The analysis supports a scoped, retrospective association in these tasks, critics and optimizers. It does not support a causal claim, a threshold at 0.5, graded prediction within a task/critic family, or prediction for unseen tasks or critics.

The training-feedback batches and the separate 128-seed outcome map below support inspection of training signals and collected-trajectory composition. Checkpoint trajectories on the fixed 512-seed evaluation bank are reported in main-paper Figure 2 and Appendix B.

Appendix L Additional Critics, Initialization Controls and Development Results

The following studies have separate protocols and are not pooled into the 512-seed primary endpoint. They record additional coverage, independent training replication and development configurations.

L.1 RoboReward and Natural Policy Gradients

RoboReward uses the frozen teetone/RoboReward-8B model and its original five-level progress rubric: eight frames, 2 fps metadata, greedy decoding and at most 12 generated tokens. A parsed score s∈{1,…,5}s\in\{1,\ldots,5\} becomes (s−1)/4(s-1)/4, and high original reward means s≥4s\geq 4. A continuous-answer diagnostic is not treated as this reward.

This third original critic uses a separate 80-component DDIM8 support, jitter .05.05, noise bound 1.5 and 300-step drawer execution. PPO uses eight rounds of 32 feedback episodes per objective. Its complete R84 endpoint has uniform/oracle/original/product successes 9/24/10/25 out of 32. Original reward changes by −.015625-.015625 with interval [−.046875,0][-.046875,0]; success changes by +1[−4,6]/32+1[-4,6]/32. It does not induce the hacking seen under the stronger natural-gradient update. Ordinary task improvement under its product cannot be counted as repair of induced exploitation.

For the natural-gradient pressure test (Kakade, 2001), all three objectives share a fresh uniform batch of 32 executed trajectories. With pi=1/80p_{i}=1/80 and gi=B−1∑j:Ij=iA^jg_{i}=B^{-1}\sum_{j:I_{j}=i}\widehat{A}_{j}, the categorical Fisher equation is solved by di=gi/pid_{i}=g_{i}/p_{i}. Every objective applies the single step pi′∝exp⁡(log⁡pi+8​di)p^{\prime}_{i}\propto\exp(\log p_{i}+8d_{i}) without clipping or entropy, then receives 96 new paired executions. This is neither PPO nor DPO, and the frozen DDIM decoder is not updated. The initial R85 critic concentrates .996824 probability on one component; all 96 sampled critic executions fail.

In R85, original reward rises .10417 [.05729,.15625][.05729,.15625] and success falls 30 to 0/96; the product restores 53, below oracle’s 94. In R93, verifier false positives assign .9149 probability to a component that fails all 88 selections. R94 instead improves task success under the original critic while increasing high-score failures from 5 to 14/96; the product removes those failures and improves success to 84. Rewarded-error amplification and overall success loss are therefore different claims.

L.2 Extra Coverage and the Verifier-only Baseline

A 1,408-label drawer verifier uses the original logistic recipe plus 1,024 earlier labels, including failed R93 training feedback. Fresh R154 feedback and evaluation contain none of its fitting rows. On 96 new paired endpoints, uniform/original RoboReward successes are 35/66, while oracle, old product, expanded product and expanded-only each achieve 95, with identical physical outcomes. This confirms an easy fresh-feedback case; it does not repair the failed R93 policy update.

R156 instead reapplies the enlarged head to the same failed feedback. Product success improves from 3 to 45/96 and high-score failures decrease from 11 to one. Verifier-only reaches 54 successes, nine more than the product. This is a supervised repair of a known failure, with 1,024 extra labels, not a new independent training or evidence of additional original-reward benefit. The cube 2,536-label head’s separate 2,080-label increment is reported in Table 17; larger supervision is not treated as a free algorithmic improvement.

L.3 Drawer LIV: Scale, Partial Progress and Closing

Exact saved-state replays of 20 objective/round combinations in the two original-scale PPO trainings reproduce their eight Adam steps exactly. Independently setting entropy to zero or normalizing advantages increases the update KL in all five original-LIV batches. Larger distribution change is not itself evidence of physical improvement. R187/R188 then test an explicitly frozen normalized protocol; their different seeds and renderer backends do not isolate normalization or rendering causally.

Only R187 supports a binary-success loss, and R188 does not repeat it. All four improve mean partial target opening and favor upper closing. Original-scale R182/R178 do not establish hacking; their products reach 53/48 successes, compared with 57/53 under identical-only. The paired product-minus-only differences are −4[−8,−1]/64-4[-8,-1]/64 and −5[−10,−1]/64-5[-10,-1]/64. R187/R188 products and only reach 63/58; equal success counts are not an equivalence test. GRPO product/only successes are 59/61 and 56/57. R179 product-minus-only target opening is −4.57​[−10.26,−.053]-4.57[-10.26,-.053] mm. None establishes an added original-LIV success benefit.

L.4 Ceiling-limited supervised initialization

To test for amplification from a reward-naive policy, we declared, before any launch, three Robometer and three terminal-oracle trainings from a supervised-only checkpoint of the same diffusion policy. It was fine-tuned only by supervised learning on the 350 successful middle-drawer demonstrations, each rendered with and without a visual occluder, with no critic and no reinforcement learning. It is not a one-factor removal of critic exposure: its observation encoder and normalizer differ from the shared warm start, so it is run with its own architecture checkpoint, and frozen-verifier scores on its features are not interpreted. All other settings are copied from critic 3, and the endpoint protocol is unchanged. This checkpoint does not solve the evaluation scene. Under the training sampler it opens the distractor in all 128 endpoint executions without a success (mean distractor opening 62.9 mm). With no success and every execution already a wrong-object failure, neither branch of the declared amplification criterion can be met: the control is ceiling-limited.

The single terminal-oracle training received almost no reward (4 successes in 5,040 training episodes) and did not establish learnability under the fixed protocol: 0/128 successes before and after, 128 and 127 wrong-object failures, and a completion change of +.0001​[−.0001,+.0004]+.0001\,[-.0001,+.0004]. The three Robometer trainings raised Robometer from .164 to .550, .580 and .501 (+.386​[+.309,+.460]+.386\,[+.309,+.460], +.416​[+.341,+.485]+.416\,[+.341,+.485], +.337​[+.263,+.411]+.337\,[+.263,+.411]; pooled +.380​[+.300,+.457]+.380\,[+.300,+.457]) while success stayed at 0/128 and wrong-object failures at 128/128 in every training, so both pooled physical changes are exactly zero and the pooled completion change is 0.0​[−.0002,+.0003]0.0\,[-.0002,+.0003]. Against the terminal-oracle training on the same seeds, their Robometer gains are +.282​[+.211,+.352]+.282\,[+.211,+.352], +.311​[+.247,+.374]+.311\,[+.247,+.374] and +.232​[+.159,+.306]+.232\,[+.159,+.306], with no difference in success, completion or distractor opening: part of the gain is specific to optimizing Robometer rather than to fine-tuning from this checkpoint. This is score amplification on persistently unsuccessful executions, not an additional wrong-object amplification result. Because wrong-object failures start at their ceiling, the control neither establishes amplification from a reward-naive policy nor establishes that prior critic exposure is necessary for it. After the first terminal-oracle training received almost no reward, we cancelled the other two; this was an outcome-informed allocation of compute, not a pre-declared futility rule, and it leaves an asymmetric design of three Robometer trainings and one terminal-oracle training.

L.5 Independent training repetition

Six further trainings use the same supervised initialization and selected layout with fresh training seeds, two per objective on one execution host and one on a second. They are evaluated on the same 512-seed bank as the primary supervised comparison and reported with it in Table 5.

L.6 Development Methods and Negative Results

The common endpoint matrix follows method development rather than random task sampling. The following distinct experiments constrain the claims; their intermediate tuning panels do not add independent replications.

Direct denoiser oracle PPO updates 1,315,847 final-convolution parameters with a uniform noise-component prior. After 768 feedback episodes and 48 updates (jitter .2.2, state-value baseline fitted to earlier feedback), fixed-endpoint success is 16/64 versus the original decoder’s 14/64: +2[−2,6]/64+2[-2,6]/64 by paired-bank bootstrap. Completion changes by .0143​[−.0494,.0797].0143[-.0494,.0797]. This control does not establish oracle learning.

A second development update reuses the first 128 of these feedback episodes with no new training feedback and changes the estimator rather than the budget. Denoising steps t=99t=99 to 1010 keep the frozen parent decoder, steps t=9t=9 to 00 use an updated final-convolution head with the same 1,315,847 parameters, all 16×716\times 7 intermediate latents and noise draws are reparameterized, and the PPO density is computed only on the executed t=0t=0 slice (4×74\times 7 of the 16×716\times 7 output). On the same batch this executed-density estimator raises the ratio of mean gradient norm to standard-error norm from .855 under full-chain sampling to 1.332, and the median split-half gradient cosine from −.132-.132 to .336.336; all 8 PPO steps are accepted. On 64 new paired seeds the original network and the final head succeed 7/64 and 8/64 (+1[0,3]/64+1[0,3]/64); completion changes by .0006​[−.0315,.0293].0006[-.0315,.0293], wrong-object failures are 13 and 12/64 (−1[−3,0]/64-1[-3,0]/64), and mean target opening changes by 1.333​[−1.308,4.932]1.333[-1.308,4.932] mm. The original Robometer score on the same 128 endpoints changes from .3295 to .3261 (−.0034​[−.0259,.0183]-.0034[-.0259,.0183]), with means .4224/.4518 on successful trajectories, .8110/.8252 on wrong-object failures and .1725/.1671 on other failures. This is one development update on reused feedback, not a training repeat: it establishes neither learned-reward hacking nor mitigation on the neural decoder, and the wrong-object reward vulnerability remains reachable.

The same executed-window estimator is then driven by fresh on-policy feedback: six rounds of 128 new feedback episodes per round, each sampled with the current window head at steps t=9t=9 to 00 and the frozen parent at t=99t=99 to 1010, followed by up to 8 KL-capped PPO steps per round with Adam state carried across rounds. Three independent histories run on two render backends (A on EGL, B and C on OSMesa); 17 of the 18 rounds accept all 8 steps and the fifth round of B accepts 2. Each history ends in one fixed endpoint of 64 new paired seeds against its original network. Paired success is 9/64 to 7/64 (−2[−6,2]/64-2[-6,2]/64) for A, 15/64 to 13/64 (−2[−5,0]/64-2[-5,0]/64) for B and 9/64 to 10/64 (+1[−2,4]/64+1[-2,4]/64) for C; completion changes by −.0200​[−.1075,.0527]-.0200[-.1075,.0527], −.0444​[−.1076,.0127]-.0444[-.1076,.0127] and .0286​[−.0228,.0808].0286[-.0228,.0808]; wrong-object failures move from 13 to 12/64, 11 to 13/64 and 18 to 15/64. The equal-weight pooled success difference is −1[−3,1]/64-1[-3,1]/64 and is descriptive only, since the two backends are different render strata. Training-batch successes per round out of 128 are 21, 23, 19, 19, 17, 13 for A, 32, 22, 26, 25, 23, 34 for B and 23, 31, 25, 24, 15, 24 for C; these are unpaired descriptions of the feedback batches, not endpoints. The pre-declared rule counts the oracle as learnable only if at least two of the three histories show a success-difference lower bound above zero or a completion-difference interval excluding zero; no history meets either condition. This is the seventh exploratory weight-level configuration. Together these configurations do not establish a statistically resolved improvement in task success and therefore do not validate a weight-level positive control; they neither demonstrate nor rule out reward hacking under neural policy finetuning. These configurations predate the full-denoiser protocol of Section 4.1, which uses a different sampler, feedback budget and credit estimator and does establish weight-level learnability.

Analytic source-bank controls.

Earlier complete-noise priors optimize pi∝exp⁡(ri/.02)p_{i}\propto\exp(r_{i}/.02) over every source component, with frozen decoder and new physical executions. Three independent RoboReward source banks give uniform/oracle/critic/product successes 28/80/26/81 out of 96; three Robometer banks give 3/36/21/47 out of 48. Original-reward means change .4922 to .5807 and .3893 to .8131, respectively. Rewarded errors can increase while the target task also improves. These analytic updates are not iterative PPO/GRPO or DPO and are reported separately from the 20 main trainings.

Appendix M Additional Verifier, Continuation and Temporal-evidence Analyses

The comparisons retain matched verifier-only rewards and their label budgets. Ball placement is a controlled extension about process evidence for outcome verification; it is not a third task under the main wrong-object protocol.

M.1 Verifier-only Ablation

The ablation removes the original critic and optimizes RV=pθR_{V}=p_{\theta} with the identical verifier, labels, policy capacity and update protocol. Supplemental same-head controls retain the original seeds and repeat uniform executions to check reference reuse. They are paired ablations, not independent training replications. Table 17 retains every available matched control and marks missing controls explicitly.

Source of the hacking repairs.

For drawer Robometer GRPO, verifier-only reaches 55 and 53/64 successes with zero wrong-object errors, compared with product outcomes 56/0 and 52/0. Product-minus-only success differences are +1[0,3]/64+1[0,3]/64 and −1[−3,0]/64-1[-3,0]/64. For distinct-color LIV stacking, expanded-only reaches 63/57 successes under PPO and 50/55 under GRPO; the product reaches 63/57 and 52/52. Neither optimizer establishes an additional physical benefit from retaining LIV. In the second PPO training, product and only have identical outcomes on every paired seed. These controls attribute much of the repair to verification without establishing a universal advantage or statistical equivalence between the two rewards.

M.1.1 Retaining the Original Reward on Normal Tasks

The value of the original reward differs from hacking repair. In three distinct-color Robometer PPO trainings, the original critic already learns the intended task, reaching 60, 61 and 58/64 successes. The 456-label product reaches 61, 62 and 57, compared with 48, 45 and 46 under the identical verifier alone (Table 24). Product-minus-only success gains are 13​[9,16]13[9,16], 17​[13,21]17[13,21] and 11​[6,16]11[6,16] per 64. Wrong-object errors decrease by 16, 16 and 15, with each interval excluding zero. These results support retaining useful original task information. They are not three additional hacking repairs. Near-color superiority does not repeat consistently.

GRPO exposes the boundary. In the first training, the small product loses 17 distinct-color successes relative to original Robometer and has no established advantage over matched-only. In the second, the product reaches 57 successes and five identity errors versus 46/14 under original reward. Its matched 456-only follow-up reaches 44/18, giving product advantages of 13​[8,18]/6413[8,18]/64 successes and −13[−18,−8]/64-13[-18,-8]/64 errors. The near-color comparison is unresolved: 34/24 versus 37/24. All 128 repeated uniform executions match the original reference. Because this follow-up was selected after the second result and uses its original seeds, it is a matched ablation, not independent confirmation of a GRPO advantage (Section K.4).

The larger head is not uniformly better. In the first Robometer GRPO training the expanded product reaches 37/64 near-color successes with 23 errors, against 24 and 33 for the smaller product and 28 and 31 for critic-only training; the second training does not repeat that repair. Its distinct-color expanded product reaches 49 successes, eight fewer than the smaller product ([−14,−2]/64[-14,-2]/64), despite 2,080 additional labels. Complete comparisons retain these costs and failures (Section K.4).

M.2 Endpoint Image Interventions and Actual Verifier Inputs

The R187 image diagnostic retains all 64 final original-LIV executions. Recorded actions reproduce initial states and all 19,200 joint steps exactly; captured preintegration poses recover every original terminal image pixel for pixel. Six terminal variants per execution keep the earlier seven frames, other joints and frozen float32 LIV scorer fixed. Unchanged native scores reproduce with maximum error zero. Setting target opening to 120 mm lowers native reward in all 64 states, by .003560–.016642. Restoring the upper drawer to its initial 57 mm opening lowers reward in 63/64. The target and upper effects interact: partial target progress has different reward effects at observed and initial upper positions. This is an image-scoring intervention, not an additional executed policy, a reachable action counterfactual, or identification of a training-time causal effect.

Verifier recomputation.

The verifier receives recorded policy-camera embeddings, not these critic-camera images. Recomputing its actual late-five-plus-initial input on all 960 R182/R183/R187 endpoint traces exactly reproduces every verifier and product score. Among 53 R187 matched seeds where oracle succeeds and LIV fails, original LIV misranks 52 pairs; verifier and product both correct 50 of those and retain two errors. Across all ten arm pairs within each of the three trainings, their ranking signs agree on every success-discordant pair. This locates the observed binary-ranking correction in the verifier, without establishing an extra original-LIV contribution or identical downstream policy updates.

M.3 Confidence-floor Intervention

Under GRPO, a trajectory with small positive reward can have positive group-relative advantage if its peers score lower. With nonnegative group rewards, zero reward has nonpositive advantage. A fixed confidence-floor intervention in R176 sets products with verifier probability below the existing .5.5 threshold to zero, retaining matched reference conditions and the same head without a threshold sweep. All 480 training and 384 final executions complete. Distinct-color Robometer wrong-object failures decrease from 12 to seven/64 relative to the old product, with a reliable interval; success changes from 52 to 54 with an interval crossing zero. Near-color no-stack failures increase. The corresponding complete LIV R177 intervention does not establish an increment over its original product. No new labels are added, and neither experiment is a new independent training repetition of the main method.

M.4 Temporal Evidence and Online Release Optimization

Physical placement followed by drawer closure was qualified using actual actions, then used for window-dependent scoring controls. Visual heads fit on 64 controls and evaluate on 64 additional executions from 16 new perturbed starts, containing 26 successes and 38 failures. Both full-history and last-quarter heads classify all 64 correctly. A subsequent matched table-camera-only ablation, reusing these controls, preserves perfect classification. The terminal images therefore contain usable outcome evidence; history’s necessity is not established.

Sixteen of the 26 successes receive exactly zero from last-quarter RoboReward. Multiplication cannot make those scores positive, and retains the 40.625% strict failure-preference rate, including 22 reversed within-start pairs. Neither critic assigns a failure a high score in either window. These are executed physical controls and static reward tests, without learned-policy hacking induction or demonstrated RL mitigation.

Ballot placement with independent terminal posture.

A separate physical task places a red ball into the middle of three opaque ballot boxes. Fixed terminal robot poses initially allow both visual windows to classify outcomes. We therefore vary the robot’s actual final joint target independently of the release action: each home joint receives a uniform ±.05\pm.05 rad offset, reached through joint-position control after release. A 64-execution development check preserves the entire ball trajectory exactly while changing the terminal arm posture. No simulator state is overwritten.

Independent confirmation retains all 14 release settings across 16 new initial ball positions and independent terminal postures: 112 training and 112 test executions, with 24 successes in each split. Both visual heads use the same frozen encoder, 64 uniformly spaced frames, and logistic fit; the windows cover the whole episode or its final quarter. The terminal window begins after the physical return motion.

The AUROC advantage is .282 [.244,.315][.244,.315], using 20,000 paired bootstrap draws over the eight test position/posture groups. This establishes a benefit from retained process evidence under this protocol, not complete terminal unobservability. Original Robometer scores, each using eight frames, have test AUROC .738 for the full episode and .656 for the final quarter. Selecting one release setting by its training-only mean final-quarter reward picks a physically reachable failure: it succeeds 0/8 on the test positions, with mean original reward .0904. Product and verifier-only selection each succeed 8/8 (original reward .0473); oracle selection also succeeds 8/8. Full-window Robometer also selects the failing release by its training mean: test reward is .2537 with 0/8 successes. Thus retaining history benefits the fitted verifier, but truncation alone does not explain the original critic’s failure preference.

Online PPO with the frozen full-history head.

We optimize a categorical selector over these 14 scripted release actions, starting each of O/C/P/VO/C/P/V from the uniform distribution. Each objective receives eight rounds of 32 fresh physical executions; the original reward uses eight last-quarter frames, while the frozen verifier uses 64 full-history frames. PPO uses eight epochs per round, Adam learning rate .1, clipping .2, batch-normalized advantages and entropy coefficient .01. The head is fitted only on the separate 112-execution calibration split above. No new labels are added to it. The selector’s logits are trainable; the motor scripts and visual networks are fixed.

After the eighth update, U/O/C/P/VU/O/C/P/V execute 64 new paired initial-position, terminal-posture and action-sampling seeds each. All 1,024 training and 320 endpoint trajectories per training history are retained. We repeat the complete protocol with independently seeded feedback and evaluation, freezing this repetition before observing the first endpoint. Both histories reuse the same calibrated head. Sampling probabilities and old log probabilities are saved before execution; every PPO update starts with zero reconstructed log-probability error.

Original-reward optimization raises the original score by .0258 [.0171,.0347][.0171,.0347] and .0299 [.0190,.0429][.0190,.0429] relative to uniform. Success differences are −10[−17,−3]/64-10[-17,-3]/64 and −7[−15,1]/64-7[-15,1]/64: the second history repeats the direction but does not resolve the success loss. The critic-trained policies select the failing release in 53 and 52/64 endpoints. Oracle raises both success and the original score; the latter differences are .0081 [.0007,.0145][.0007,.0145] and .0085 [.0028,.0139][.0028,.0139]. Product restores 61​[57,64]/6461[57,64]/64 and 59​[54,63]/6459[54,63]/64 successes relative to critic training. Intervals use 20,000 paired endpoint bootstrap draws conditional on each trained policy, not a training-population confidence interval. Product and verifier-only have identical binary outcomes within each history, so these experiments do not establish an additional benefit from retaining the original reward. These results establish online reward exploitation and physical recovery within this scripted action family, not end-to-end neural VLA mitigation or an exclusively temporal cause of native-critic failure.

Matched online window ablation.

For each history we repeat product training with the final-quarter head fitted on the same 112 labels, using the same 64-frame count, encoder, initialization, PPO budget and all physical and sampling seeds. This adds 256 feedback and 128 U/PU/P endpoints per history; repeated UU verifies runtime matching and does not count as a new independent baseline. Both first batches reproduce all 32 action and physical traces, native-input PNGs and original scores exactly; repeated UU endpoints also match. Full-history products succeed 63 and 64/64 versus 17 and 2/64 for final-quarter products. Paired differences are 46​[39,53]/6446[39,53]/64 and 62​[59,64]/6462[59,64]/64. Original-score differences between the two products have intervals containing zero in both histories. Thus process evidence materially improves this verifier’s online mitigation at equal label and frame budgets; the first quarter-window run still partially improves on uniform. This intervention does not establish that truncation alone causes the original critic’s failure.

M.5 Continuing from Exploited Checkpoints

This separate drawer Robometer/PPO protocol retains all three frozen parent histories R82/R87/R88. Each continuation copies the parent’s logits and Adam state, reuses the same 24-component support and 384-label R59 verifier, and collects eight rounds of 24 fresh feedback episodes per objective. The shared first batch gives 696 unique training executions per parent. No labels are added. Fixed checkpoint 008 is evaluated on 64 new paired seeds per arm in the original opening .475 and the prespecified opening .375, held out from continuation. The decoder remains fixed.

All three completed ID panels independently retain the reward–success conflict at their exploited starting points: relative to current uniform, original reward rises by .5125, .4834, and .3516, while success falls by 9.375, 17.188, and 10.938 percentage points; all six paired intervals exclude zero. Product continuation improves success over its frozen parent by 89.063 points [79.688,96.875][79.688,96.875], 75 points [64.063,85.938][64.063,85.938], and 20.313 points [10.938,29.688][10.938,29.688]. Wrong-object failures fall from 58 to zero, 57 to four, and 56 to 30/64. Continuing the original reward produces 60, 57, and 54 wrong-object failures. The equal-parent ID success rates are 5.73% for the exploited starting points, 5.21% for continued original reward, 67.19% for the product, 68.75% for verifier-only, and 86.98% for oracle. Product-minus-parent repair is 61.46 points [55.73,66.67][55.73,66.67]; this mean includes the incompletely repaired third history.

The same-label verifier-only controls succeed 61, 49, and 22/64. Product-minus-only success differences are zero (identical paired outcomes, so the bootstrap interval degenerates to [0,0][0,0]; zero discordant pairs in 64 still allow a discordance rate up to 4.6% at one-sided 95%, and this is not an equivalence result), 4.688 points [−4.688,14.063][-4.688,14.063], and −9.375-9.375 points [−18.750,−1.563][-18.750,-1.563]. The third history favors verifier-only; the equal-parent difference is −1.563-1.563 points [−5.729,2.604][-5.729,2.604], which does not establish an extra product benefit or policy equivalence. At opening .375, the same fixed product policies improve success from 12, 8, and 7/64 to 62, 49, and 21/64. Gains are 78.125 points [67.188,87.500][67.188,87.500], 64.063 points [48.438,78.125][48.438,78.125], and 21.875 points [9.375,35.938][9.375,35.938], while wrong-object failures fall 41→\to0, 37→\to0, and 39→\to16/64. Equal-parent success rises from 14.063% to 68.750%, a 54.688-point gain [46.875,62.500][46.875,62.500]; continued original reward achieves 17.188%. No labels, refitting or policy updates are added for this test opening. All three transferred exploited parents have higher original reward and more wrong-object failures than uniform; only R88 resolves a binary success loss, so this is a transfer test of repair from ID-exploited policies, not three new strict hacking inductions.

Verifier-only reaches 62, 38, and 23/64 at the held-out opening. Product exceeds verifier-only in R87 by 11/64 [5,17]/64[5,17]/64, ties R82, and has an unresolved −2/64-2/64 difference in R88. The equal-parent success difference is 4.688 points [1.042,8.333][1.042,8.333], but wrong-object differences and the ID controls do not support universal product superiority. All intervals use 20,000 paired-bank draws within each fixed parent, not population uncertainty over training histories.
